chapter_theme: Kakapusundar opens his Njanam by collapsing the whole of yoga into one place, the crown of the egg (அண்டவுச்சி), reached by fixing the mind at the uvula so that the breath subsides upward. Against it he sets everything else as waste: the counted supports and places, mantras, nose-tip gazing, tongue-raising hatha yoga, Vedas and Puranas, temples, tirthas and flower pooja. A cosmology of sun, moon and fire twining down one nerve from the crown to the two eyes carries the method.
structure_note: Invocation and the teacher's announcement to his disciple Vasimuni (2326 to 2330); the crown, the nerve and the three lights (2331 to 2337); against mantras, with the sign of the unspoken letter (2338 to 2340); kalpa, samadhi and the forehead eye (2341 to 2346); against ritual, ending with the uvula method that the chapter has been circling (2347 to 2350). Every verse begins with the last word of the one before (அந்தாதி).

2326.reading: We bow to the Being-Consciousness-Bliss that, as the supreme Parapara everywhere, became sun, moon and fire, let the five elements and maya appear, made countless crores of eggs, became endless lives, showed its form even as the differing faiths, and rose and stands in the egg.
2326.nuance: ரவிமதியுஞ் சுடர்மூன்று, sun, moon and fire as three lights, is the image the whole work returns to (2333, 2337, 2395, 2404); tradition takes them as the two breaths and the fire at the centre of the body as much as as cosmic lights. மதபேதமாகவுந்தான் வடிவைக் காட்டி makes the sects themselves forms the One takes, which softens the attacks on sects that follow.

2327.reading: The teacher announces that, having gone in the sushumna at the crown of the egg beyond the city where Om ends, with name gone, he will set out yoga-jnana and make clear collyrium and tilaka, medicine, the eight karmas and the whole art called alchemy, and show the seed of true knowledge.
2327.nuance: The verse is a table of contents: அஞ்சனம் (collyrium, a siddhi of sight or invisibility, delivered in 2402), வயித்தியம் (medicine, 2400), அட்ட கர்மம் (the eight magical acts) and வாதம் (alchemy, 2397 to 2399). காமென்ற வீடம் is obscure; it may be the house of desire or a corrupt word.

2328.reading: He will tell the way called yoga: hold the five senses within the Supreme; whoever, without knowing, talks sects, fails to reach the holy crown, and says the supports are many and the places twelve, stacked one on another, talks bravely and wastes away; look with desire on the egg that drank poison.
2328.nuance: The attack is on chakra-doctrine itself: counting ஆதாரம் and பன்னிரண்டு தலங்கள் is set against the one place. விடமுண்ட அண்டம் is unclear; it may recall Siva who drank the poison, so that the crown is his throat, or be a corrupt phrase.

2329.reading: Every place is the crown of the egg; go to the lotus at the eighteenth tier, lock the mind there without slipping and enter Brahman for good: there there are no mantras, no fate, no intellect, no destiny; it will dawn when the mind is one, so stay pure and do tapas.
2329.nuance: பதினெட்டாங் கோடு, the eighteenth tier, is not explained; the sixteen kalas of the moon plus two, or a count of the lotus's levels, are the usual guesses. மதியில்லை can be 'no intellect' or 'no moon', the moon-breath having ended; the verse's run of negations reads either way.

2330.reading: Listen, son Vasimuni: in the thousand verses he gave earlier he told truly the drugs, salts, bound and melted substances and the way of gems, without a lie; in this book he will tell all the silence in order, so listen bowing.
2330.nuance: The disciple is வாசிமுனி, the breath-sage, and later வாசிநாதா; the name makes the pupil the breath itself. The earlier ஆயிரம் is an alchemical work claimed as Kakapusundar's; the verse marks the turn from alchemy to மவுனம், which the formulas of 2397 to 2403 then undo.

2331.reading: Khechara is the crown of the egg; for those who see it firmly it becomes silence; call it Parabrahma yoga; as it is stacked, awareness is lifted high; the khechara gem, bindu and nada thicken and gather; daily one can see the whole egg dancing with Shakti and hear the sound of anklets.
2331.nuance: கேசரம் is the khechari of hatha yoga, there a tongue seal; here it is a place, the crown, which prepares the rejection of the physical tongue-practice in 2350. கெவுனமணி is obscure (perhaps the sky-gem). The anklet sound is the inner nada, as tradition has it.

2332.reading: In Brahman one can see the certainty: standing in the crown of the egg it produced the sense-organs, created the crop of lives in the world for ever, became the seven kinds of birth called the bond and the four kinds of womb, and so the eggs are endless upon endless.
2332.nuance: ஏழுவகைத் தோற்றம் and நாலுவகை யோனி are the standard classifications of births and wombs. The body-crown and the cosmic egg are one word, அண்டம், so creation is told as happening in the head.

2333.reading: In the middle of Brahman came sun, moon and fire as three; divided they twine and flow downward; he tells the light in the two eyes: beyond the tip of the crown a nerve hangs like a banyan's aerial root, twines straight into the two eyes, and becomes light and fills them.
2333.nuance: The anatomy is coded: the நரம்பு from the crown to the eyes, the three lights flowing down it. Tradition reads the eyes as the seats of sun and moon; the plain picture is of the optic path, which the next verse calls the three-part sushumna in the skull.

2334.reading: When the light of Parabrahman flows along the nerve-way in the ten, it becomes light in the two eyes and the whole egg appears as one; the nerve, the hanging root's circle, becomes the three-part sushumna in the skull; he will tell more for the ear and the tongue.
2334.nuance: பத்திலே is unexplained (ten nadis? ten breaths?). முக்கூறாய்ச் சுழுனை puts the sushumna, usually the spinal channel, in the skull and gives it three parts, perhaps the three lights.

2335.reading: In the root, in the linga, the nerve runs from below upward along the staff and by the nape path, well through the nerve, rising as high as the egg's top; joined with the nerve named before it twines and becomes the brow-centre.
2335.nuance: மூலம், லிங்கம், தண்டு and பிடர் மார்க்கம் are the perineum, the genital, the spine and the nape; the verse traces the central channel without naming kundalini. தமர்போலே (like a hole, or like a drill) is unclear.

2336.reading: What is the brow-centre: it is the crown of the egg that is Parabrahman; the middle of the nerve named before is fixed as the sushumna; when you drive the mind straight at the uvula, the mind leaps into the sushumna and the five elements merge as one.
2336.nuance: Brow-centre, crown, sushumna and uvula are made one place in four lines; the method is to send the mind, not the tongue or the breath, to the அண்ணாக்கு. This is the verse that 2339 and 2350 enforce.

2337.reading: Through the nerve named before the sun, moon and fire fill, twine and flow downward; when one looks at the inner one they subside; we have said openly the gaze of the Nadanta Parabrahman; the bindu too is the crown of the egg: plant the chitta there firmly.
2337.nuance: ஓமடா opens the last couplet as the syllable and as an exclamation. நாதாந்தம், the end of sound, is one of the six ends; the verse claims to tell openly what is usually hidden, a claim 2393 repeats against other siddhas.

2338.reading: The crown of the egg is the ocean in which the fourteen worlds show through the Supreme; this is the way of silence where the siddhi of siddhas plays; when were the mantras born, when did Vishnu and Brahma come, when did the three gunas arise? See the sign of the unspoken letter.
2338.nuance: The questions place mantras, gods and gunas after Brahman, so none can be the way to it. கூறாத அட்சரத்தின் குறி, the sign of the unspoken letter, recurs (2358, 2394): a letter that is not spoken, which the verse offers in place of mantra.

2339.reading: They do not see: were gracious mantras born before Brahma arose? Learning endless mantras without seeing, staring at the nose-tip and calling it the sushumna, wandering in vain like madmen, they perish root and all, worthless cattle; only those who know the sign and look straight at the uvula have release.
2339.nuance: A polemic against nasikagra-drishti, gazing at the nose-tip, which other schools take as the seat of the sushumna; Kakapusundar moves it to the uvula. மூக்குநுனி and அண்ணாக்கு are set against each other as false and true place.

2340.reading: Release: when you think a mantra the mind splits in two; truth is the mind alone as one, sitting apart and pushing away sleep; if the intellect enters Brahman the whole earth will bow to you; not wandering in deceit, the breath that climbs the nape path is itself the kalpa.
2340.nuance: The objection to mantra is psychological: a mantra makes a second thing in the mind. கற்பம், the rejuvenating preparation of the medical siddhas, is redefined as the ascending breath, so that 2341 can speak of drinking it.

2341.reading: When one drinks the honey that is the kalpa called self, its name is sanchara samadhi; the flesh's hunger ends and anger goes; going to the hill of rising and piercing through, the seven screens called honey burn away; for those who go to the centre of the crown all the instruments called king subside and one can watch Death's dance.
2341.nuance: சஞ்சார சமாதி, the samadhi of moving about, is the siddha's waking absorption (also 2376). உதயகிரி, the hill of rising, is a cipher for the crown or the brow. கூற்றுவனாராட்டம் can mean watching Yama's play from safety or seeing Death's dance ended; the sense turns on whether ஆட்டம் is defeat or performance.

2342.reading: One can see: one leg (or wind) is raised high and sings, one is let down; the one that looks upward is named moon, son, and the one that looks downward you may take as sun; and above the crown of the egg, on the way, is the dwelling of the great fire.
2342.nuance: கால் is both leg and wind. Plainly the picture is the dancer with one foot raised; as cipher, tradition takes the upward wind as the moon-breath and the downward as the sun-breath, with fire at the crown. Both readings stand, and the verse seems to intend both.

2343.reading: Not knowing this, siddhas gathered and said there are sixty-four yogas in the world, each different, and wandering they perished, endless crores; one who looked at raja yoga, knew the state and saw is one in a crore; without speaking, with the mind's eye, see the space, the place where the bindu leapt.
2343.nuance: ராசாங்க யோகம், raja yoga, is here the yoga of the mind set at one place, against sixty-four counted methods. The sixty-four match the sixty-four arts and attainments elsewhere in the tradition.

2344.reading: Having seen with the eye all unseen sights, he got the name Kaka Pusundar; wandering a while unseeing, he approached the Brahman called the pole and asked, and it told him without shame to seek in the crown of the egg with the mind and look unbending, and he fixed the mind as one without flinching.
2344.nuance: The teacher's own guru is Brahman itself, துருவம், the fixed pole; no human lineage is given until 2389. The etymology of காகபுசுண்டர் is left to the reader; the crow form is explained in 2373.

2345.reading: Fixing the mind as one in the heart, setting there as one the thing that is supreme bliss, staying filled in nirvikalpa samadhi for many crores of years, when he opened the forehead eye and looked the whole earth was filled as one; so fix the thought as one, remove the door and see the Cause and play.
2345.nuance: லலாடக்கண், the forehead eye, is the inner sight that 2362 develops. கபாடம், the door or bolt, is in tradition the closed passage at the crown (brahmarandhra). The heart (இருதயம்) appears as the place of fixing, against the crown elsewhere.

2346.reading: Playing and becoming awareness, seeing the light of the uncut wheel, knowing the brow eye in the stable egg, removing the serpent's venom, unwavering, kin to no one, pushing off the lure of the jewelled woman, taking Brahman alone as companion, hold the mind in check as silence.
2346.nuance: வெட்டாத சக்கரம், the uncut wheel, recurs in 2350; it may be the wheel of the crown or the unbroken circle of light. அரவு விடம், the serpent's venom, is read by tradition as kundalini's poison, or plainly as the venom of the senses; the verse does not decide.

2347.reading: Told to stand, men of the world will not settle into fixity and samadhi; like experts they will recite Vedas, Puranas, kavyas and crores upon crores of mantras, and saying temple and tirtha they wander about, thieves and hollow; not knowing the one Brahman-state that wins, they fall like a tree without root.
2347.nuance: திருடர்கள், thieves, is the word for pilgrims; the image of the rootless tree makes the state of Brahman the root and all texts and shrines the foliage.

2348.reading: Taking flowers and setting up a linga they do not bow to the ... linga; bathing it and doing pooja the vain ones bawl; when you pluck the flower it has become like a dead body, so see clearly; those who with the mind see within the Supreme have the body of Kailasa.
2348.nuance: பார்த்தீப லிங்கம் is unclear (perhaps பார்த்திப, the linga of earth or of the king, or the luminous linga; the sense of the line depends on it) and கத்தபம் is obscure. The plucked flower as a corpse is the verse's own argument: an offering is a killing. கயிலாசத் தேகம், the Kailasa body, is the siddha's perfected body.

2349.reading: Not approaching the Brahman that is self, saying the gods on earth are endless and this one a guru and that one a disciple, cattle that never saw the hill of rising, doing lies, theft and murder, lusting after prostitutes and becoming vain, such a one will not reach the guru's feet; he will fall into hell.
2349.nuance: The verse condemns both the multiplication of gods and the guru-disciple relation as ways of not approaching Brahman, yet ends by making the guru's feet the goal; 2357 resolves this by making guru and disciple marks of the one Brahman.

2350.reading: Those who raised the tongue to the uvula and gazed got no result; the eyes burst and the body goes; they call it hatha yoga, and it is not fit; set the mind straight at the uvula and look: the breath subsides above and does not look downward, and one can know the uncut wheel.
2350.nuance: அடயோகம் is hatha yoga and the practice rejected is khechari mudra, the tongue turned back to the palate. Kakapusundar keeps the place and changes the instrument: the mind, not the tongue, goes to the uvula, and the breath then stays above of itself.

links.note: Tirumular tells the practitioner to mark the adharas that have been taught and find the one letter above the fifty in the welling adhara; Kakapusundar says that whoever counts the supports as many and the places as twelve wastes away, since every place is the one crown. The conflict holds if 2328 attacks the doctrine of several centres, not merely talk without practice.

Tirumular makes the five letters the seat of Nandi and the chakra within which he sits; Kakapusundar says that in Brahman at the crown there are no mantras at all. The two clash if 2329 denies mantra as a way; if it only describes the state after arrival, Tirumular could agree.
2329 states that there are no mantras in Brahman; 2340 gives the reason: a mantra thought makes the mind two, and the way is the mind alone as one.

Both make the breath held high in the head the cure for ageing: Tirumular's two breaths set in the upper palate undo grey hair and wrinkles, Kakapusundar's breath climbing the nape path is the kalpa itself.

Both reduce the many methods to a few that matter: Tirumular's twenty thousand eight hundred kinds of karma, mantra and yoga give only toil and come down to four; Kakapusundar's sixty-four yogas ruin crores while raja yoga saves one.

Tirumular says that if the ordained temple pujas lapse disease grows, rain fails and kings weaken; Kakapusundar calls those who wander saying temple and tirtha thieves who fall like rootless trees. The conflict is over whether temple worship holds the world up or holds the seeker back; it stands on any reading of 2347.

Tirumular says pearl, ash, rice, flowers or sand can all be made the linga, the Father's body, by one who seeks to be saved; Kakapusundar says setting up a linga and plucking flowers for it offers a corpse and gets nothing. Both speak of the same act, outward linga worship; one makes it a way and the other a waste.

Both move the linga inside: Tirumular makes the heart the temple and the soul the Sivalinga for those who are clear; Kakapusundar gives the Kailasa body to those who see within the Supreme with the mind rather than bowing to a set-up stone.

Tirumular says that if the tip of the tongue is pressed up into the middle, soul and Siva dwell there and the flesh does not die for a hundred crore years; Kakapusundar says those who raised the tongue to the uvula got nothing, their eyes burst and the body went, and the mind alone should go there. Same place, opposite verdicts on the physical seal.

new_concepts.gloss: Brahman: the Supreme (also பரப்பிரமம், பராபரம்) from which gods, lives and eggs issue and into which mind, breath and worlds are absorbed; Kakapusundar's name for the goal of the whole practice
new_concepts.label_source: Used in nearly every verse, as பிரமம் (2329, 2340), பரப்பிரமம் (2334, 2336) and பராபரம் (2326, 2364)

new_concepts.gloss: the crown of the egg: the top of the head taken as the summit of the cosmos, the one place where body and universe are the same egg and where the mind is to be fixed
new_concepts.label_source: Used as அண்ட வுச்சி in 2327, 2329, 2331, 2336, 2337, 2338, 2342, 2344 and throughout the work

new_concepts.gloss: sushumna, the central channel, which Kakapusundar places in the skull at the brow-centre and the uvula rather than along the spine
new_concepts.label_source: The verses write சுழுனை (2327, 2334, 2336, 2339, 2353); சுழுமுனை is the standard form

new_concepts.gloss: the breath as the practice: the breath driven or allowed to climb the central way and subside at the crown; the disciple is himself named after it
new_concepts.label_source: Used in 2340, 2350, 2377, 2385, 2387; the disciple is addressed as வாசிமுனி (2330, 2332) and வாசிநாதா (2365, 2380)

new_concepts.gloss: kalpa: the rejuvenating preparation of the medical siddhas, which keeps the body from ageing, and the inner practice that is said to replace it
alchemy: the art of transmuting metals (also வேதை), with its drugs, salts and calcined preparations
new_concepts.label_source: Used in 2327 as வாதமென்ற வித்தை and in 2399 as வேதையென்ற வித்தை; 2330 names its materials

source_issues: 2327: காமென்ற வீடமதிற் is obscure and may be corrupt.
2328: விடமுண்ட அண்டமதை is unclear; the sense of the last line depends on it.
2348: பார்த்தீப லிங்கத்தை and கத்தபம்போற் are unexplained words, possibly corrupt.
2347: புரா ணங்காவ் யங்கள் is split oddly across the metrical break (புராணங் காவ்யங்கள்).
